Activity Description: The purpose of this project is to work with Spanish gill net and trawl fishers to reduce mortality and injury to accidently captured sea turtles along the Spanish Mediterranean coast. Activities include: 1. continue evaluation of sea turtle bycatch in artisanal fisheries operating out of three Valencia community ports using on board observers; 2. continue analysis of maritime recreational fishing and sea turtle bycatch; 3. engage 22 fisherman associations to prepare a strategy for reduction of sea turtle bycatch from fishing vessels operating out of Valencia community ports; and 4. supporting awareness, education and outreach efforts directed towards fishing communities including publication of The Turtle Gazette, published with topics for fisherman practical interest as well as sea turtle conservation messaging

Activities include: (1) continue evaluation of sea turtle bycatch in artisanal fisheries operating out of three Valencia community ports using on board observers; (2) continue analysis of maritime recreational fishing and sea turtle bycatch; (3) engage 22 fisherman associations to prepare a strategy for reduction of sea turtle bycatch from fishing vessels operating out of Valencia community ports; and (4) supporting awareness, education and outreach efforts directed towards fishing communities including publication of The Turtle Gazette, published with topics for fisherman practical interest as well as sea turtle conservation messaging.

Funding Account Name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Resource Management
Activity Name: Education and Training to CITES Authorities in Central America and the Caribbean
Activity Description: The purpose of this project is to counter wildlife trafficking in Central America and the Caribbean by capacity development in several countries of the region on the implementation of CITES. This will be done by facilitating the successful selection, mentorship, and graduation of students in a Masters Course on CITES. Key intended results include the graduation of a co- hort of students, and the subsequent strengthening of CITES Authorities in the region.Specific activities will include: (1) facilitating the successful selection, mentorship, and graduation of students on the mentioned Masters Course. (2) coverage of all logistic needs of students: traveling from their countries to Spain and back, accommodation, maintenance, academic taxes, simultaneous interpretation English- Spanish, small economic support for thesis field work, health and accident insurance.

Implementing Partner Name: U.S. Government - Department of the Air Force
Funding Account Name: Department of the Air Force, Operations and Maintenance
Activity Name: Inter-European Combat Search and Rescue Course - Spain
Activity Description: This one week course, conducted at the Tactical Leadership Programme in Albacete, Spain, establishes foundational knowledge and understanding of CSAR Doctrine as well as Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures for junior aircrew, CAOC, SOF and Intel personnel. It aims to provide broad, generalized awareness of Combined Air Operations Combat Search and Rescue operations to tactical operators to enable them to more readily integrate into future combined air operations and exercises. The course provides a brief overview of CSAR doctrine, architecture, and the roles of key CSAR players with special emphasis on planning and execution considerations of CSAR in a combined air operations environment.
